main_text.head: QUAESTIONES PERTINENTES AD VIAM judicandi vitiosa argumenta.

head.i: An sola sophismata & decipularum strophae sint Elenchi: & utrum dicantur Elenchi agendi an patiendi significatione?

main_text.p: VOx Elenchus est in polysemis. Interdum significat Indicem: quomodo librorum Elenchos appellamus. Hęc significatio à nostro instituto aliena est. Interdum argumentum vel argumentationem ipsam denotat. In hac significatione, quæ Dialectica est, duo sunt eius genera: Unum verum, ut philosophicum & logicum: alterum sophisticum & captiosum, quod Aristoteles etiam vocat ἐριστικὸν [?], id est, litigiosum, & ἀγωνιστικὸν [?], id est contentiosum & rixans. page.notes: The woodcut initial is read as "V" (joined to "Ox" as "VOx"); the letter is partly obscured, so please check it. Greek words marked [?] are read from a small, faded print and may be wrong in their accents or letters. The line ending "(in-" is the catchword; the next page presumably begins "instrumentum" or similar, which I have not transcribed. The page number "119" is printed at the top right. The signature "H 4" is at the foot left.
